description: Invite payload container (`spindle-invite-v1`, DESIGN.md §A4 "Invites" and A10.46): the pasteable blob that carries a signed `invite`-kind capability together with everything a fresh client needs to reach the registry it names — ordered endpoints and how to authenticate the registry's TLS. Unsigned as a container, like A4's bootstrap bundle: the capability inside carries the signature, so the container has no domain tag and no signing input. Each case pins both the canonical CBOR and the unpadded-base64url transport form.

cases.name: web_pki_two_endpoints
cases.description: The baseline invite: an `invite`-kind capability naming the invitee's root_fp as `subject` (A10.46 — invites are addressed, not bearer), two registry endpoints in preference order, and public-web-PKI TLS validation.

cases.name: private_ca_root
cases.description: Hardened variant: the registry presents a certificate chaining to exactly this DER-encoded root and nothing else. Pins the `PrivateCaRoot` arm's `{kind: 1, root}` encoding against `WebPki`'s `{kind: 0}` — the `root` key is absent, not null, when the pin is web PKI.

cases.name: endpoint_boundary_length
cases.description: Edge case: one endpoint at exactly the decoder-enforced byte-length cap (MAX_ENDPOINT_LEN = 256). The strict decoder must accept exactly this length and reject one byte more. The cap is on UTF-8 *bytes*, so a TypeScript reader measuring `String.length` (UTF-16 units) would disagree with Rust on non-ASCII input.

cases.name: max_endpoints
cases.description: Edge case: exactly MAX_ENDPOINTS (8) endpoints — the most a decoder accepts. Ordering is meaningful and preserved: a client tries them most-preferred first.

cases.name: private_ca_root_alphabet_edges
cases.description: The alphabet case. Its private CA root cycles `fb ff bf`, which encodes to the repeating quad `-_-_` — base64 indices 62 and 63, the only two that differ between RFC 4648's standard (`+`/`/`) and URL-safe (`-`/`_`) alphabets. Every other case here is built from `rep()` runs of one repeated byte, and none of them reaches either index, so without this case the corpus would pin the encoding without ever pinning the alphabet — the one thing the `base64url` field exists to pin. `invite.test.ts` asserts the corpus contains both characters, so deleting this case fails loudly rather than silently narrowing coverage.

cases.name: tls_pin_boundary_length
cases.description: Edge case: a private CA root at exactly MAX_TLS_PIN_LEN (2048) bytes, the largest the decoder accepts. Also the largest invite this vector set encodes — note its size is NOT a capacity measurement, since the embedded cap's `op_cert` here is a 16-byte dummy pattern rather than a real one (see MEASURED_INVITE_BYTES).
